name: Mensa
introduction: is the Table Mountain, named by Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille after the flat-topped mountain overlooking Cape Town, where he observed the southern sky in the 1750s. It is the only constellation named after a feature on Earth.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Mensa is the faintest constellation, with no star brighter than fifth magnitude. Lacaille chose the name because the Large Magellanic Cloud, which extends into Mensa, reminded him of the clouds that often cover Table Mountain.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Gamma Mensae](hip:25918) is an orange giant about 100 light-years away, and [Mu Mensae](hip:21949) a blue-white giant. Pi Mensae, a Sun-like star, hosts the first planet discovered by the TESS space telescope.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The edge of the Large Magellanic Cloud extends into Mensa, along with several of its star clusters.
